title: Adding and subtracting fractions
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review
markup: {3/4} shows as a stacked fraction; {1 3/4} as a mixed number.

sections.title: Find a common denominator
sections.objective: Find a number both denominators divide into.
explain: To add or subtract fractions, the pieces have to be the same size. {1/2} and {1/3} are different-size pieces, so you can't count them together yet.
A common denominator is a number both denominators divide into evenly. Then both fractions can be cut into pieces of that size.
Multiplying the two denominators always works. For {1/4} and {1/6}: 4 × 6 = 24. A smaller one keeps the numbers easier: count by 6 (6, 12, ...) until you reach a number 4 also divides into. 12 works.

visual.caption: Cut both bars into the same number of pieces. Which numbers of pieces work for both?

sections.title: Rewrite over the common denominator
sections.objective: Rewrite a fraction with a new denominator without changing its value.
explain: Once you have a common denominator, rewrite each fraction so it has that denominator.
Ask: what do I multiply the old denominator by to get the new one? Then multiply the numerator by the same number. For {1/4} = {?/12}: 4 × 3 = 12, so 1 × 3 = 3, and {1/4} = {3/12}.
This works because multiplying the top and bottom by the same number is multiplying by 1 ({3/3} = 1). The amount stays the same. The pieces just get smaller, and there are more of them.

visual.caption: Cut each fourth into 3 pieces. The shaded amount doesn't change.

sections.title: Add or subtract the numerators
sections.objective: Add and subtract fractions that already have the same denominator.
explain: When the denominators are the same, the pieces are the same size. Add or subtract the numerators to count the pieces.
The denominator stays the same, because it tells you the size of the pieces, and that doesn't change. {2/7} + {3/7}: 2 sevenths plus 3 sevenths is 5 sevenths, {5/7}.
Adding the denominators would change the size of the pieces. {1/2} + {1/2} is one whole, not {2/4}.

visual.caption: Put the shaded pieces together. Count the pieces. Did their size change?

sections.title: Simplify the result
sections.objective: Write an answer in simplest form.
explain: A fraction is in simplest form when no number bigger than 1 divides both the top and the bottom.
To simplify, find a number that divides both, and divide the top and bottom by it. {6/8}: 6 and 8 are both even, so divide both by 2 to get {3/4}. Keep going until nothing else divides both.
If the top and bottom are the same, the answer is 1. If the bottom becomes 1, write just the whole number.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: Add and subtract fractions with different denominators, start to finish.
explain: Adding or subtracting fractions with different denominators takes four steps.
1. Find a common denominator. 2. Rewrite both fractions with it. 3. Add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator. 4. Simplify.
Example: {1/4} + {1/6}. A common denominator is 12. {1/4} = {3/12} and {1/6} = {2/12}. Then {3/12} + {2/12} = {5/12}, which is already in simplest form.
sections.scaffold: In guided practice, each of the four steps gets its own answer box. In the mastery problems, the student does all four steps alone.

hints.frac.add-sub.common-denom: Count by the bigger denominator until you reach a number the smaller one divides into. Or multiply the two denominators.
hints.frac.add-sub.rewrite: What do you multiply the old denominator by to get the new one? Multiply the numerator by that same number.
hints.frac.add-sub.combine: Keep the denominator. Add or subtract only the numerators.
hints.frac.add-sub.simplify-result: First add or subtract the numerators. Then look for a number that divides both the top and the bottom.
hints.frac.add-sub: Start with step 1: what's a common denominator for these two fractions?

simplifyHint: That's the right amount, but it isn't in simplest form. Is there a number that divides both the top and the bottom?

misconceptionMessages.frac.add-denominators: Adding the denominators doesn't give a common denominator. You need a number both denominators divide into evenly. Try counting by the bigger one.
misconceptionMessages.frac.larger-denominator: The bigger denominator only works if the smaller one divides into it evenly. Does it here? If not, keep counting by the bigger denominator.
misconceptionMessages.frac.additive-scaling: Adding the same number to the top and bottom changes the amount. Multiply the top and bottom by the same number instead.
misconceptionMessages.frac.numerator-unchanged: When the denominator gets multiplied, the numerator has to be multiplied by the same number, or the amount changes.
misconceptionMessages.frac.add-across: The denominator is the size of the pieces. Adding gives you more pieces of the same size, so the denominator stays the same. Add only the numerators, and only once the denominators match.
misconceptionMessages.frac.subtract-across: The denominator is the size of the pieces, and subtracting doesn't change that size. Subtract only the numerators, and only once the denominators match.
misconceptionMessages.frac.numerators-not-scaled: You found a common denominator, but the numerators have to change too. Multiply each numerator by the same number you multiplied its denominator by.
